pins.name: GPIO0
pins.label: GPIO0
pins.notes: Must be HIGH or floating for normal boot; LOW at boot enters flash/programming mode. No interrupt support. Commonly wired to a FLASH/BOOT button on dev boards

pins.name: GPIO1
pins.label: GPIO1
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 TX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: GPIO2
pins.label: GPIO2 (Led active low)
pins.notes:
Must be HIGH at boot. Onboard LED (active-low, LED_BUILTIN) - confirmed via official ESPert library source + Cytron's own V2 test-jig firmware, see chipGpios note
Onboard LED (active-low) — see pfodWeb NOTE above pinNotes for sources

pins.name: GPIO3
pins.label: GPIO3
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 RX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: GPIO13
pins.label: GPIO13 (Button)
pins.notes:
Onboard USER button (active-low, INPUT_PULLUP) - confirmed via official ESPert library source, see chipGpios note
Onboard USER button (active-low, INPUT_PULLUP) — see pfodWeb NOTE above pinNotes for sources

pins.name: SS
pins.label: SS (GPIO15)
pins.notes: Must be LOW at boot (tied to GND via resistor on most boards)

pins.name: GPIO16
pins.label: GPIO16
pins.notes: RTC-domain pin: no internal pull-up/down, no PWM, no interrupt support. Commonly wired to RST for deep-sleep wake

pins.name: A0
pins.label: A0 (GPIO17)
pins.notes: Analog input only (A0) — cannot be used for digital I/O or PWM. No V2-specific schematic or spec confirms an on-board divider (unlike V1's vendor blog, which stated a 3.3V max for its AD pin) - defaultRefVolts left at the bare chip's native 0-1.0V, see adc note below
